Name of patient: Rogers, Pamela

Heading: Symptoms and Descriptions

Symptom 1: Chest pain
Description: Abrupt onset of dull, aching chest pain for the last week, beginning in the left parasternal area and radiating to the neck. First episode occurred while working in the garden after about 45 minutes of exertion and fatigue, lasted 5 to 10 minutes, and resolved with rest inside in a cool area. She has had 2 additional similar episodes, including one while walking her dog that lasted 15 minutes and resolved with rest, and one that woke her from sleep and lasted 30 minutes, prompting her Emergency Department visit. Pain is associated with shortness of breath, but not with sweating, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, palpitations, movement, food, GERD symptoms, or palpable tenderness.

Symptom 2: Shortness of breath / dyspnea
Description: Occurs with the chest pain episodes. She reports no other exertional dyspnea, orthopnea, or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea.

Symptom 3: Epigastric pain / burning
Description: Complains of epigastric pain with a burning quality approximately twice a month, primarily at night.

Symptom 4: Lower back pain
Description: Aching lower back pain approximately once every week after working in her garden, usually relieved with Tylenol.

Heading: Severity Report

Severity report: High

Reason: The chest pain is recurrent, exertional, and now occurring at rest and awakening her from sleep, which is concerning for unstable angina / possible ischemic heart disease. This severity is inferred from the clinical picture in the document rather than explicitly stated.

Description: Burning epigastric pain occurring approximately twice a month, primarily at night.

Description: Aching lower back pain occurring about once every week after working in her garden, usually relieved with Tylenol.

Symptom 5: Hypertension
Description: History of hypertension diagnosed 3 years earlier; blood pressure on exam was 168/98. She previously stopped an unknown medication after 6 months because of drowsiness.

Symptom 6: Systolic murmur
Description: Grade 2/6 systolic decrescendo murmur best heard at the second right intercostal space and radiating to the neck.

Symptom 7: Crackles in lung bases
Description: Crackles were heard in the lung bases bilaterally on chest exam.

Symptom 8: Third heart sound
Description: A third heart sound was heard at the apex.

Symptom 9: Abdominal bruit
Description: Bruit heard in the right paraumbilical area.

Symptom 10: Cystic changes of breasts
Description: Cystic changes noted in both breasts without masses or nipple discharge.

Severity report: #High

Reason: The patient has exertional and rest chest pain with radiation, associated shortness of breath, and progression in frequency/duration, which is concerning for unstable angina or myocardial ischemia. The report also documents hypertension, abnormal cardiac and lung exam findings, and a strong family history of premature coronary artery disease, all of which increase concern. Severity is inferred from the pattern of symptoms and the need for emergency evaluation.
